# Cross-deployable writes: how each one reaches its owner

**Generated by `python tools/check-cross-deployable-writes.py --write`; do not edit by hand.** The routes are `x-ticvai-write-via` on each operation in `contracts/` (copied into `handoff/api-data-lineage.json` as `writeVia`); the kernel grants and the exceptions are `docs/active/cross-deployable-writes.yaml`. ADAM CR-002 on DB-ROLES, decided by Chinmay on 12 October 2026 (CHG-R6-020).

**Why.** DB-ROLES gives each deployable's PostgreSQL role DML only on the schemas its own modules own (ADR-0055; `handoff/service-decomposition.json`). A write into another deployable's schema made with the caller's own SQL is refused at runtime. ADR-0055 rule 4: across deployables a write travels by event (ADR-0057) or by the owner's published HTTP operation. Within one deployable, rule 3 stands: call the owner module's in-process API inside your transaction.

## How to build each route

- **event `<name>`**: write the event to `platform.outbox` in the same transaction as your own change (ADR-0033). The owning module's consumer (in the `workers` host, its idempotency key in the event file under `events/`) performs the write; the consumer that does it lists the table under `writes`. Your operation does not touch the table.
- **operation `<operationId>`**: call the owner's published operation over HTTP with an `Idempotency-Key` derived from your own record's id, so a retry is safe. The owner's write is in the owner's transaction, not yours.
- **exception `XDW-nnn`**: the write cannot route yet. DB-ROLES grants the writer's role DML on that one table until the removal release; the reason says what removes it.

| | writes |
|---|---:|
| Cross-deployable writes in the lineage (62 operations) | 71 |

## The kernel tables every deployable is granted directly

| Table | Privileges | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `platform.outbox` | INSERT | Every host writes the events it emits in the same transaction as the change they report (ADR-0033, ADR-0058). |
| `platform.scope` | SELECT | Every host resolves the caller's scope and its row-level security reads it (ADR-0005). Read only: a write to platform.scope from another deployable is not exempt. |
| `platform.audit_record` | INSERT | Every operation that audits itself appends its audit row in its own transaction (CHG-R6-002). |
| `platform.idempotency_record` | SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE | Every host claims, completes and replays an Idempotency-Key in the transaction of the write it guards. |
| `platform.outbox_sequence` | SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE | Every host allocates the next sequence of the aggregate it changes, in the transaction that writes the outbox row (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... RETURNING), so a sequence survives the outbox's monthly partitions leaving (ADAM CR-166, 18 October 2026; CHG-CRA-005; ADR-0057 and ADR-0058 as amended). DB-ROLES grants it to commerce, access, operations and workers. |
| `platform.tenant_field_key` | SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE | The kernel in every host encrypts, decrypts and blind-indexes for the current tenant (KERNEL-FIELD-ENC), so every host reads the tenant's wrapped keys, creates a missing one on first use (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) and moves a rotated one to decryptOnly; never deleted (ADAM CR-339, 30 October 2026; CHG-CR339-001; ADR-0063 as amended that day). DB-ROLES grants it to commerce, access, operations and workers. |
| `platform.blind_index_rehash` | SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE | A lookup on a re-hashable blind index, in whichever host makes it, reads whether its column's re-hash is finished, and the kernel's re-hash job records its progress (ADAM CR-339, 30 October 2026; CHG-CR339-001). DB-ROLES grants it to commerce, access, operations and workers. |

Every other table in another deployable's schema is reached by one of the routes below.

## Reads granted across deployables

A deployable's role may SELECT these tables although another deployable owns them, and asks the owner's named queries in process (ADAM CR-196, decided by Chinmay on 21 October 2026; ADR-0055 rule 4 and DB-ROLES as amended). Row-level security still applies; the grant reaches existing databases in the forward migration tools/derive-ddl.py writes.
